elements.element: Customer owns Deliverables and work product created for Customer.
elements.evidence: New § 2(e) is a licence grant only ("TrueLink hereby grants to Client a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free license to use, modify and sublicense all results of the Support Services and any other work product prepared for Client hereunder"). No provision vests title to the work product in Client, and § 2(d) ("TrueLink retains all of its ownership and license rights in the Interface") is left intact.

elements.element: Vendor assigns the Deliverables and work product to Customer.
elements.evidence: No assignment language appears anywhere in the rendered text; the only new operative words are a licence grant in § 2(e). Preferred would require e.g. "TrueLink hereby assigns to Client all right, title and interest in all results of the Support Services and work product prepared for Client hereunder."

elements.element: Vendor retains its pre-existing intellectual property.
elements.evidence: § 2(d) is retained unchanged: "Notwithstanding the license granted under section 2.1, TrueLink retains all of its ownership and license rights in the Interface."

elements.element: Customer's licence to Vendor IP embedded in Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: § 2(e) grants a "perpetual" licence over "all results of the Support Services and any other work product prepared for Client hereunder", expressly "Notwithstanding section 2(d)", so it reaches TrueLink-owned material contained in that work product.

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: § 2(e) uses the word "irrevocable" and overrides § 2(d) ownership retention for the licensed results/work product.

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: § 2(e): "perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free license"; no additional fee or royalty is imposed elsewhere in the rendered text.

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data.
elements.evidence: Nothing in the redline states that Client retains all right, title and interest in Client data. § 10(c) only deems "Client's Intellectual Property, all results of the Hosting and Support Services" to be Client Proprietary Information, which is a confidentiality classification, not an ownership allocation. To reach preferred, insert a standalone sentence vesting all rights in Client data in Client.

elements.element: The parties do not jointly own intellectual property.
elements.evidence: Condition inapplicable: no joint-ownership language exists in the document. § 2(d) allocates Interface ownership solely to TrueLink and new § 2(e) creates only a licence in Client's favour, so nothing creates co-ownership.

elements.element: Vendor may retain ownership of generic tools and know-how.
elements.evidence: Favourable-to-Vendor but checklist-permitted language is preserved: § 2(d) "TrueLink retains all of its ownership and license rights in the Interface", and § 2(e) is framed as a licence "Notwithstanding section 2(d)", so Vendor's platform, tools and know-how ownership survives.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: § 2(e) expressly grants a "perpetual" licence to "all results of the Support Services and any other work product prepared for Client hereunder". § 2(c) ("The license shall last until this Agreement is terminated") reads on the capital-L Interface "License" granted in § 2(a) (cf. § 4: "the License granted under Section 2"), so it does not defeat the new grant, but see the drafting note in reasons.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: § 2(e): "perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free license" - the word "irrevocable" appears in the operative grant.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is worldwide.
elements.evidence: § 2(e) states the licence is "worldwide"; no territorial restriction is imposed elsewhere in the rendered text (the § 2(a) field-of-use limit applies to the Interface licence, not to § 2(e)).

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: § 2(e): "royalty-free license"; no separate consideration is attached to the grant.

elements.element: Customer may use and modify Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: § 2(e): "license to use, modify and sublicense all results of the Support Services and any other work product prepared for Client hereunder in Client's business."

elements.element: Customer may sublicense Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: § 2(e) expressly includes the right to "sublicense" the results and work product "in Client's business".

reasons: Fallback level is position-complete: new § 2(e) supplies all five licence attributes (perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free) plus the use, modify and sublicense rights over "all results of the Support Services and any other work product prepared for Client hereunder", and unchanged § 2(d) satisfies the Vendor-retains-tools element.

Preferred level is not reached: there is no assignment/ownership of the work product to Client and no Customer Data ownership sentence. That is acceptable here because the drafter expressly targeted the fallback and the fallback is fully met; the finding is correctly classified as a deviation because the pre-redline text gave Client only a use-only licence to the Interface terminating with the Agreement (§ 2(c)) and nothing at all over the paid-for programming work product.

Drafting tightening (non-blocking): § 2(e) opens "Notwithstanding section 2(d)" only. Because § 2(c) is headed "Term" and says "The license shall last until this Agreement is terminated", an expressio unius reading could be argued against the perpetual grant. Repair by expanding the carve-out to "Notwithstanding sections 2(c) and 2(d)" or adding "This license survives any expiration or termination of this Agreement."

Scope alignment (non-blocking): § 10(c) speaks of "all results of the Hosting and Support Services" while § 2(e) covers "results of the Support Services". The catch-all "and any other work product prepared for Client hereunder" should capture hosting outputs, but mirroring "Hosting and Support Services" would remove any argument that hosting deliverables are outside the licence.

Minimality confirmed: one concise new subsection, no deletion or duplication of existing operative terms, no requirements imported from outside the fallback checklist (no assignment, no Customer Data clause, no cap or extra covenant added).

Intent preserved: TrueLink's ownership of the Interface (§ 2(d)), the Interface licence and its field of use (§ 2(a)), the Interface licence term (§ 2(c)), the Support Services obligation (§ 4) and the confidentiality treatment (§ 10(c)) all survive without contradiction; § 2(e) grants rights only, it does not divest Vendor title.
No walk-away trigger is present, consistent with the rationale: no Customer IP or Customer Data is assigned to TrueLink and no joint ownership is created.
